title: Geostationary velocity expression
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be expressed as v = (13.2πR)/T or an equivalent simplified form.

title: Acceleration at perigee expression
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be expressed as a = (gR²)/(R+h)² or an equivalent simplified form.

title: Correct orbital radius
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the geostationary orbital radius as R + 5.6R = 6.6R for the velocity calculation.

title: Newton's law application
description: Important: The solution must apply Newton's law of gravitation (F=GMm/r²) to relate the satellite's acceleration to the gravitational field.

title: Elimination of GM
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the surface gravity relation (g = GM/R²) to eliminate the product GM from the acceleration equation.

title: Circular motion relation
description: Optional: The solution may explicitly state the relation between linear velocity, radius, and period (v=2πr/T) for the geostationary orbit.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The solution may include a check that the final expressions have correct units for velocity and acceleration.

title: Incorrect radius for acceleration
description: Pitfall: Using an incorrect orbital radius (e.g., using 5.6R instead of 6.6R, or using h incorrectly) in the acceleration or velocity formulas.

title: Sign or algebraic error
description: Pitfall: Making an algebraic mistake when solving for acceleration, such as incorrectly inverting the radius ratio or misplacing a squared term.
